identity.name: resolve_bylaws
identity.description: Layer 2 by-law resolution (Spec 134): for every in-population residential parcel, runs the Spec 68 evaluator per structure x target x class and records the winner, why the others lost, the status and the inputs used, as one row per lot holding every result as a positional array in scope-seed order, with two closed dictionaries for unit ids and texts (CHAT-80.QP option 4). MATERIALIZER ROWS form: the runner pages parcels and writes the three tables in one transaction per batch. Layer 3 (compute_maxbld_scenarios) reads only these rows.

why_lock.text: Spec 47 §A.5: the spec number is globally unique (130 for link_parcel_abutments); mutual exclusion with every other writer of the bylaw_resolution_* tables. The shell keeps `const ADVISORY_LOCK_ID = 134;` as a source-text constant, asserted equal by the pipeline advisory-lock suite.

write_discipline.scope: unit_key referenced by a lot of this run (content-addressed)

why.text: CHAT-80.QP (option 4): the closed dictionary of unit ids, keyed by hash32 of the unit id (first four bytes of its sha256); a stored entry never changes under its own key, so a re-run rewrites nothing.

write_discipline.scope: text_key referenced by a lot of this run (content-addressed)

why.text: CHAT-80.QP (option 4): the closed dictionary of reason, evidence-ref and permission texts, keyed by hash32 of the text; content-addressed, so a re-run rewrites nothing.

guard_why.text: A keyed delete: every key in replace_keys is deleted outright (R-IU: a parcel that left the population loses its link row); nothing to compare.

write_discipline.scope: parcel_id = ANY(<the batch's out-of-population parcel ids>)

why.text: Spec 124 R-IU (ratified Q-L2-4): the existing replace-keys write retracts the link row of a parcel that left the population; written before the guarded upsert of the same table in the batch transaction. A deleted parcel takes its row by ON DELETE CASCADE.

write_discipline.scope: parcel_id of this run's in-population lots

why.text: Spec 134 §3, R-IU, CHAT-80.QP: the lot row, one per in-population parcel, holding all of its results as positional arrays in scope-seed order; written after the replace-keys retraction of the same table in the batch transaction.

invalidates.when: Layer 1 (table_version), the evaluator code (evaluator_version), a parcels input the lot vector reads, or the population list changes. why.text: Per batch, one transaction, the four statements of outputs.writes[] in order: the two dictionary upserts (parents first), the replace-keys retraction and the lot upsert.

LDG-10 producer edge (watermark, not evaluated): zoning_class, zoning_zn_string, exception_number, zoning_overlays, zoning_is_ambiguous, on_policy_road and in_sixplex_area are enrich_parcels' outputs; re-read every run under the full rescan.
LDG-10 producer edge (watermark, not evaluated): is_corner_lot, is_through_lot and abuts_laneway are enrich_centreline's outputs; re-read every run under the full rescan.
LDG-10 producer edge (watermark, not evaluated): is_heritage_designated is enrich_heritage's output; re-read every run under the full rescan.

Migration 282 enables RLS on bylaw_resolution_units with ZERO policies (Spec 114 Class B). Under a non-bypass role the guarded upsert affects 0 rows with NO error, so the counters read 0 and the verdict reads PASS (R-CT).

Migration 282 enables RLS on bylaw_resolution_texts with ZERO policies (Spec 114 Class B). Under a non-bypass role the guarded upsert affects 0 rows with NO error, so the counters read 0 and the verdict reads PASS (R-CT).

A deleted parcel takes its lot link row (R-IU, ON DELETE CASCADE); a dropped foreign key would leave link rows for parcels that no longer exist, which the population check would then count.

pending.predicate: TRUE -- full rescan: every parcel is paged; the population split is the pure splitPopulation (R-IU)

why.text: Keyset paging over parcels.id: the step is a full rescan of every parcel (R-IU: the source pages every parcel, the pure splitPopulation sends out-of-population parcels to the retraction).

on_check_error_why.text: Every check reads a value the compute already measured (the batch tallies and the post read), so a throwing check is a defect and reddens the run.

expect.reports: parcels paged by the source, lots resolved and link rows retracted this run

why.text: Descriptive denominator of the run; INFO under the Rule 10 exception for a purely descriptive counter: violations is always 0 and the counts live in detail.

expect.reports: Spec 134 I1 and I11: |link rows - live population| plus link rows outside the population

why.text: I1: link rows equal the live in-population parcel count; I11: rows only for the population. Counted from the once-per-run post read, in the run that wrote them.

expect.reports: Spec 134 I9 (option 4): lot rows whose arrays are not one slot per scope pair, winner keys with no unit row, reason or evidence-ref keys with no text row

why.text: I9 lineage under option 4: every array has one slot per scope pair, every winner key names a stored unit of the closed dictionary, every reason and evidence-ref key names a stored text. (Signatures are gone, so "winner is a candidate" is checked as "winner is a Layer 1 unit"; the equivalence audit covers the rest.)

expect.reports: Spec 134 I2 and I8: applies rows with a winner but no clause or provincial evidence, or with no winner and neither a ruled absence nor a cited regulation (M-60 agreeing worlds, CHAT-115)

why.text: I2/I8: an applies row has a winner unit with evidence clause or provincial, or is unregulated by a ruled absence (evidence present), or (CHAT-115.L2-EVID-1, 2026-10-24) is an M-60 agreeing-worlds value with no single winner whose applied clauses share one regulation, cited as clause/provincial evidence. A ruled absence is any evaluator evidence of kind absence, label_absent or disapply (Q-D reading of "absence ruling").

expect.reports: Spec 134 I3 and I4: a result of a gated lot that is not not_evaluated or has a winner

why.text: I4: no winner on a lot with a lot gate, including the lot-wide unauthored-exception gate (Spec 134 §5).

expect.reports: Spec 134 I5: an exception-layer winner on a lot whose exception number is the sentinel

why.text: I5: a sentinel (-1) exception lot never takes an exception-layer winner.

expect.reports: not_evaluated:conflict results written this run (Spec 134 I3)

why.text: I3: a conflict is a defect, never an answer; the bound is the declared variable resolve_bylaws_conflict_max (default 0), never a compute comparison (G7).

expect.reports: Spec 134 I10: lot-vector inputs the builder had to default

why.text: I10: a missing input is never defaulted (it raises the lot gate); the counter is the builder's own, an exact zero.

expect.reports: Spec 134 I13: lot rows with more classes than resolve_bylaws_class_cap, or a class_results key that is not a declared class

why.text: I13: every class_results key is a declared class (layer2-scope.json classes) and the class count per lot is within resolve_bylaws_class_cap, passed to the post read as a parameter (Q-C).

expect.reports: results whose reason is needs_user_input on a scenario axis (Spec 134 I13; Q-F)

checks.retighten_when: zero results: the class vectors enumerate every scenario axis, then this becomes a FAIL at 0 (Spec 134 I13)

why.text: Q-F recommended reading: I13 says no needs_user_input on a scenario axis survives, but the v1 classes do not yet enumerate every axis, so the count WARNs against a declared ceiling (Spec 124 R-H: a metric that is never zero is WARN with a stated retighten condition).

expect.reports: Spec 134 I14 (Q-I): lot rows whose stored row_sha differs from the SHA-256 recomputed in SQL, and dictionary rows whose key differs from the hash of their content

why.text: I14 (operator CHAT-73, Q-I recommended reading; CHAT-80.QP): the lot canonical text is built in SQL from the same result columns the JS hashes (rowShaMismatchSql), and each dictionary key is the SQL hash of its content; a direct row edit is detected.

expect.reports: Spec 134 I12: audited pairs whose direct per-lot effective() differs from what the lot row decodes to (every class)

why.text: I12 (Q-N): every Nth lot is re-evaluated uncached for every structure, target and class and compared with what its row decodes to; the sample size is the budget because pure compute holds no clock (R-DET).

expect.reports: Spec 134 I15: audited pairs whose result changes when the candidate order is reversed

why.text: I15 (Q-N): the audited lots are re-evaluated with the candidates in reversed order; the evaluator's declared total order makes the result independent of it, so any difference is a defect.

expect.reports: Spec 134 I12 coverage: 1 when lots were resolved but no pair was audited (detail: pairs audited)

checks.retighten_when: the first POST capture fixes resolve_bylaws_equivalence_every_nth against the population: a run that audits nothing then FAILs

why.text: I12: a run that audited no pair proves nothing; WARN (not PASS-by-silence) until the sample size is sized from the first POST measurement (R-AJ).

expect.reports: percent of results written this run that are not_evaluated; detail carries the reasons (Spec 134 §7 WARN)

checks.retighten_when: the first POST capture measures the share: set resolve_bylaws_not_evaluated_warn_pct to the measured share plus margin (Spec 124 R-H)

why.text: Spec 134 §7 WARN: the not_evaluated share, bounded by the declared variable (interim 100, never warns until measured).

expect.reports: applies winners by layer (base, overlay, exception, provincial); detail carries the histogram (Spec 134 §7 WARN)

why.text: Spec 134 §7: the winner-layer histogram, purely descriptive; INFO under the Rule 10 exception, violations always 0 and the histogram in detail.

expect.reports: unit and text dictionary rows no longer referenced by any lot after a law change (Q-M)

checks.retighten_when: a pruning arm lands (Q-M): stale dictionary rows are then deleted by the run and this becomes a FAIL at 0

why.text: Q-M recommended reading: dictionary rows are never deleted by the run (no destructive retraction at v1), so a law change leaves unreferenced entries behind until the reset arm rebuilds; the count makes that visible.

expect.reports: Spec 134 I6: lots gated by an unauthored exception, counted live in the same run; detail carries every gate

why.text: I6: the gated-lot count is a live count from the run's own table, never census.json; INFO under the Rule 10 exception (a descriptive counter): violations always 0, the count in detail.

expect.reports: measured size in MB of the three Layer 2 tables (Spec 134 §6, R-JA)

why.text: Spec 134 §6 and R-JA: the tables' measured size against resolve_bylaws_storage_budget_mb at POST; over budget the lean split is re-cut before ③, never a silent growth. The value 1300 in limit is the interim seed (Q-K).

limitations.what: Dictionary rows (units, texts) are never deleted by a run: a law change writes new entries under new keys and leaves the old ones unreferenced until the reset arm rebuilds the layer (Q-M).
limitations.measured: declared: the unreferenced_rows check counts them; the recovery.reset truncates all three tables

limitations.what: losers, inputs_used and disclosures are not stored (CHAT-80.QP): they are recomputed on read through the uncached evaluator, and a class that differs from the first class stores only its differing positions (class_results).
limitations.measured: declared: locked by materialize.logic.test.ts and frozen-row.logic.test.ts; the equivalence audit compares every class against what the lot row decodes to

limitations.what: Scenario axes the v1 classes do not enumerate still surface as not_evaluated:needs_user_input (Q-F).
limitations.measured: declared: counted by scenario_axis_cells against resolve_bylaws_scenario_axis_warn_max

recovery.reset: TRUNCATE bylaw_resolution_lots, bylaw_resolution_texts, bylaw_resolution_units; the next run re-derives every lot row (an operator action on a DB night, the layer is fully derivable from parcels and Layer 1).

interrupted_why.text: Each batch commits its retraction and upserts atomically in one transaction (parents before children); an interrupted run leaves earlier batches committed and the next run is a full rescan that repairs the rest.

why.text: A WARN row stands (scenario-axis results, not_evaluated share, unreferenced rows, nothing audited) and nothing FAILED.
A guards.requires precondition (RLS bypass, the lot foreign key) is missing, or a declared logic variable has no row; nothing is written.
A declared variable (including the population list) is outside its bounds with on_invalid fail: the run refuses before any write.
Advisory lock 134 is held by another process; the library emits a row-derived SKIP summary.
